dossier.public_summary: The dip is only seen in a few events and changes depth dramatically between the two TESS sectors. One transit is almost absent and the depths alternate, indicating eclipses at twice the reported 13.8-day period blended together rather than a single planet. The overall picture is a background/foreground eclipsing binary, not a planet on the target.

reasons.why: Depth changes by ~77% between sectors 57 (1464 ppm) and 84 (3325 ppm) with p_constant 0.0001078, far from consistent.
The variability is astrophysical, not a pipeline calibration difference: both sectors are TESS-SPOC and the depth differs within the same source, ruling out differenced_pipeline.

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are inconsistent; one transit in sector 57 is essentially missing (108 ppm vs ~2308 ppm mean), driving the sector difference and indicating more than photometric scatter.
reasons.value: p_consistent=2.0379247489064355e-07 chi2=33.9419117813071 dof=3 mean_depth_ppm=2308 top-3 share=1.0 outlier depth_ppm=108 sigma=-4.9 at btjd 2881.1

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses differ at ~3 sigma (1.9:1 ratio, 1711 ppm), supporting a binary at twice the folded period (27.6 d), with the deep even event matching the deeper sector 84 average.

With only 4 transits, sector depths correspond to two odd and two even events; the average per sector is not a planet average but alternating primary/secondary eclipses folded together, and a false-colour/alias harmonic is plausible.
